title: Plains and Pioneers Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the Plains Indians and the first settlers heading West along the Oregon Trail.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Plains Indians, Oregon Trail and the 1849 California Gold Rush.
final_note: You learned how the Plains Indians lived, why settlers went West, and what the Gold Rush changed.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Plains Indians depended on the buffalo.

It gave them food, clothes, tipi covers, tools and fuel. Tribes like the Sioux and Cheyenne were nomadic, moving with the herds. Land was shared — not owned.

From the 1840s settlers loaded wagons in Missouri and headed West.

The Oregon Trail was around 2,000 miles. Many died from disease, accidents or crossing the Rockies in snow — but the idea of Manifest Destiny pulled them on.

Gold was found at Sutter's Mill in California in January 1848.

By 1849 a Gold Rush brought 80,000 'forty-niners' West. Meanwhile the Mormons, led by Brigham Young, had settled around the Great Salt Lake in Utah from 1847.
